name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Hari Tua (old-age savings)
authority: PP 46/2015 art.16 — 5.7% of the monthly wage, 2% from the employee and 3.7% from the employer. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AO5` = 2% (employee) and `!AR5` = 3.7% (employer); `!AE5` prints the combined 5.7%. NO CEILING: the highest-paid local employee, basic 22,380,750, is charged `AO17` 447,615 = 2% of the FULL wage, and the one foreign employee at 62,000,000 is charged `AK6` 1,240,000 = 2% of the full wage. Both would be clamped if any ceiling applied, and neither is. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): PP 46/2015 art.17(3): wages paid by the day make a month of the day’s wage × 25, whatever days were paid (`person.terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY"`). Owner rule 2026-09-28 (ID-161): PP 44/2015 art.19(1)–(2) and PP 46/2015 art.17(1)–(2) charge JKK, JKM and JHT on “Upah sebulan” — upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap as a monthly rate — and, unlike PP 45/2015 art.29(1) for JP, do not say “pada bulan yang bersangkutan”; so a monthly-paid worker's base is the contract's monthly rate (`person.terms.monthly_wage`: the basic plus the contract allowances counting toward this scheme, on the terms in force on the month's last employed day), whatever days were paid — a joiner, a leaver and a month with unpaid days are charged on the whole rate. The law is silent on an hourly-paid worker (art.19(3)–(5) name only daily, piece and weather-bound piece wages); default: the wage paid for the month's hours. Piece-rate wages use the average paid wage of the preceding 3 months, or 12 months where work depends on weather (PP 44/2015 art.19(4)–(5), PP 46/2015 art.17(4)–(5)); only months of this employment count. The first month uses the current paid wage. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing registration does not waive this charge (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; PP 46/2015 art.2(1) obliges the employer to register every worker for JHT, art.9(2) runs the contribution from the day the worker starts, and art.11(4) makes a negligent employer pay the contribution it owed. A recipient paid outside an employment relationship — a PMK 168/2023 bukan pegawai (NON_EMPLOYEE, IRREGULAR_COMMISSIONER, ACTIVITY_PARTICIPANT), a former employee or a pension withdrawal — is not a wage-earning worker of this employer: PP 44/2015 art.5(2)–(3) and PP 46/2015 art.4(2)–(3) make a worker outside an employment relationship a non-wage-earning participant who registers and pays for himself (PP 44/2015 art.11(1)), and Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) binds the employer only for its Pekerja; so that recipient class charges nothing, the lawful exclusion a NOT_REGISTERED record no longer stands in for.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Pensiun (pension)
authority: PP 45/2015 art.28 — 3% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 2% from the employer, charged on wage up to an annually adjusted ceiling (art.29). SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AN5` = 1% (employee) and `!AQ5` = 2% (employer); `!AF5` prints the combined 3%. The ceiling and its March step are read off the one employee it binds — see ID_BPJS_CEILINGS_OBSERVED. JP covers Indonesian nationals only (the rule `when`). The one foreign employee is charged 0 in both `AJ6` and `AM6` on every (FOREIGN) sheet while still paying JHT, JKK, JKM and Kesehatan. Nationality is not a `rate_selector` axis; it belongs on employment_statutory_facts — see ID_JP_FOREIGN_EXCLUSION. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23: PP 45/2015 art.15(1)–(3): the pension age is 56, 57 from 1 January 2019 and one year more every three years — 59 from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027; art.15(4): a participant who is still employed may choose to take the pension when work stops, at most three years after pension age. Owner rule 2026-09-28 (ID-161): PP 44/2015 art.19(1)–(2) and PP 46/2015 art.17(1)–(2) charge JKK, JKM and JHT on “Upah sebulan” — upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap as a monthly rate — and, unlike PP 45/2015 art.29(1) for JP, do not say “pada bulan yang bersangkutan”; so a monthly-paid worker's base is the contract's monthly rate (`person.terms.monthly_wage`: the basic plus the contract allowances counting toward this scheme, on the terms in force on the month's last employed day), whatever days were paid — a joiner, a leaver and a month with unpaid days are charged on the whole rate. The law is silent on an hourly-paid worker (art.19(3)–(5) name only daily, piece and weather-bound piece wages); default: the wage paid for the month's hours. Piece-rate wages use the average paid wage of the preceding 3 months, or 12 months where work depends on weather (PP 44/2015 art.19(4)–(5), PP 46/2015 art.17(4)–(5)); only months of this employment count. The first month uses the current paid wage. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing registration does not waive this charge (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; PP 44/2015 art.4(1) obliges the employer to register every worker for JKK and JKM, art.8(2)–(3) runs the contribution from the day the worker starts and leaves the benefit on an employer that has not reported and paid, and art.10(4) makes a negligent employer pay the contribution it owed. A recipient paid outside an employment relationship — a PMK 168/2023 bukan pegawai (NON_EMPLOYEE, IRREGULAR_COMMISSIONER, ACTIVITY_PARTICIPANT), a former employee or a pension withdrawal — is not a wage-earning worker of this employer: PP 44/2015 art.5(2)–(3) and PP 46/2015 art.4(2)–(3) make a worker outside an employment relationship a non-wage-earning participant who registers and pays for himself (PP 44/2015 art.11(1)), and Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) binds the employer only for its Pekerja; so that recipient class charges nothing, the lawful exclusion a NOT_REGISTERED record no longer stands in for. Applied 2026-09-28 (ID-52): PP 7/2025 art.3–4 and art.10, extended by PP 36/2025 art.I angka 2 (art.10A) through the January 2026 contribution month: a labour-intensive enterprise with at least 50 workers registered as active BPJS Ketenagakerjaan participants, in the food, beverage and tobacco, textile and apparel, leather and leather goods, footwear, children's toy or furniture industry (art.3(3)–(4)), has its JKK cut by 50% for the contribution months February 2025 to January 2026, to I 0.120%, II 0.270%, III 0.445%, IV 0.635%, V 0.870% of Upah sebulan (art.4(1)); the entity fact `jkk_padat_karya` records that BPJS Ketenagakerjaan verified it (art.5(2)). authority: Perpres 82/2018 art.30 as amended — 5% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 4% from the employer, charged on wage between a floor and a ceiling (Perpres 59/2024 art.32(1) and (2) — the third amendment, in force 8 May 2024 — restating the ceiling and floor; art.31 was deleted by Perpres 64/2020 and art.30(2) is the direct-payment rule). For PPU outside micro/small enterprises, art.32(2)–(3) sets the workplace UMK, with UMP as fallback; art.32(4) excludes micro/small enterprises from that floor, and art.32(5) requires a separately determined actuarial floor; Applied 2026-09-18: `by_region` carries the Kabupaten Bekasi UMK (Kepgub Jabar 2026) beside the UMP, and the company’s region names it, so the floor is the workplace UMK. name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan (job loss)
authority: PP 37/2021 Pasal 11 as amended by PP 6/2025: the JKP contribution is 0.36% of the wage capped at Rp5,000,000 (Pasal 11(7)–(8)), of which 0.22% is the central government's and 0.14% is recomposed out of the JKK contribution the employer already pays; nothing is charged on a payslip beyond JKK. PP 37/2021 art.43 as amended by PP 6/2025 art.11, in force 7 February 2025 — 0.36% of the monthly wage, of which 0.22% is borne by the Central Government and 0.14% comes from recomposing JKK (PP 49/2023 art.16A). Only that recomposed 0.14% is an employer charge: JKK class III 0.75 + JKM 0.30 + JKP 0.14 = 1.19% of wage, the same total the source workbook's 0.89 + 0.30 charges; only the composition of the payslip lines moves. JKP covers Indonesian workers under 54 at first registration with the required social-security enrolment; contribution arrears affect benefit claims but do not establish an exemption from employer registration. Neither nationality nor JKP registration is a `rate_selector` axis; both belong on employment_statutory_facts. Applied 2026-09-18: PP 37/2021 art.4 covers an Indonesian national under 54 (`citizenship`, `age`); an eligible worker recorded NOT_REGISTERED cannot be treated as exempt from JKP registration. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Corrected 2026-09-29: PP 37/2021 art.4 as amended by PP 6/2025 art.I(1) requires an Indonesian worker under 54 at registration who has an employment relationship and the prescribed JKK/JHT/JKM/JKN (and, at medium/large employers, JP) coverage. Explicit NOT_REGISTERED for that worker refuses payroll instead of erasing the duty; a foreign national or a worker already 54 at first registration remains outside JKP. Under PP 6/2025 art.I(2), JKP has no incremental employer payslip charge: its 0.14% funding is recomposed from JKK and 0.22% comes from the government; JKK is separately assessed at its full rate.

name: Pajak Penghasilan Pasal 21 (income tax withholding)
authority: PP 58/2023 and PMK 168/2023, in force 1 January 2024 — for every tax period but the last, a permanent employee's withholding is the monthly average effective rate (tarif efektif rata-rata, TER) for the employee's PTKP category applied to monthly gross. Category A is PTKP TK/0 (54,000,000) and TK/1 & K/0 (58,500,000), 44 brackets; category B is TK/2 & K/1 (63,000,000) and TK/3 & K/2 (67,500,000), 40 brackets; category C is K/3 (72,000,000), 41 brackets — all transcribed from the PMK 168/2023 Lampiran. Employee JHT (2%) and JP (1%) are charged as their own schemes and are not read as a relief on this scheme’s base: PMK 168/2023 art.15 applies the TER to gross. The last tax period is the first rung: the annual UU PPh art.17(1)(a) progression on PKP = year gross − biaya jabatan (5%, at most 6,000,000; PMK 168/2023 art.10(2), which revoked PMK 250/PMK.03/2008 by art.24(a) — corrected 2026-09-28) − the year's employee JP and JHT (PMK 168/2023 art.10(1)(b), iuran terkait program pensiun dan hari tua kepada BPJS Ketenagakerjaan) − PTKP, PKP rounded down to the whole thousand (UU PPh art.17(4)), less the year's withholding, a negative charge being the refund. Employer-borne JKK, JKM and the 4% Kesehatan are additions to the taxable gross (`produced.<code>.employer` in `assessed_on`). Applied 2026-09-18: employer-borne JKK, JKM and BPJS Kesehatan premiums are additions to the gross (PMK 168/2023 art.5(1)); in the five labour-intensive sectors an employee with a monthly gross up to 10,000,000 has the PPh 21 borne by the government for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods (PMK 10/2025, PMK 105/2025; entity fact `pph21_dtp_sector`), so nothing is withheld from them. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): UU 36/2008 art.7(1): the PTKP dependant count is the dependants in a direct line of blood or marriage and adopted children, at most three (`employee.dependents_count`, capped), not the children on record; the `ptkp` election KI is PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): a married woman who shows the local government's written statement that her husband has no income is given PTKP for herself, the married status and her dependants — never the spouse's own 54,000,000, which UU 36/2008 art.7(1) grants only in a combined annual return, not in withholding (corrected 2026-09-23); PMK 168/2023 art.10(2): biaya jabatan is 5% to Rp 500,000 a month, so the year’s cap is 500,000 for each month employed (`year.months_employed`); PMK 10/2025 art.2: the Government-borne PPh 21 is for a gross fixed and regular income of at most Rp 10,000,000 in the month (`BASE` and the fixed allowances), not the whole taxable base; PP 68/2009: severance (pesangon, UPMK) is taxed at its own final rates and is outside the TER base; a non-resident is under PPh 26. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): UU 36/2008 art.21(5a) as amended by UU 7/2021 (HPP): the withholding rate for a taxpayer without an NPWP is 20% higher than for one who shows it — every rung, the year-end reckoning included, is multiplied by 1.2 under the PPH21 election `no_tax_id`. Since UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021 a resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP and DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024 applies no surcharge where a valid NIK is given, so the election is for a recipient with neither. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): PMK 168/2023 art.9(4) — the PTKP (and so the TER category and the December reckoning) is the status at the start of the calendar year. The PPH21 elections `ptkp_marital_status`, `ptkp_dependants` and `ptkp` are dated declarations whose later changes apply from the next 1 January (`change_effect` YEAR_START); an unrecorded year-start PTKP declaration refuses calculation. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): tax residence (UU PPh art.2(3)–(4)), the PTKP status and dependants at 1 January (art.7(2)), the tax identity (art.21(5a)) and, for a married employee, the gender are declared inputs; an unknown one stops the calculation rather than taking the resident, favourable or current-record reading. Applied 2026-09-25: PMK 168/2023 arts.12 and 16 and Lampiran A.III–VII: explicit recipient_class selects monthly non-permanent wages or irregular commissioners (monthly TER including the final month), independent services (Article 17 on 50% of eligible monthly gross), or activity participants, former-employee irregular payments and active pension withdrawals (Article 17 on full monthly gross). These classes do not use Article 15 annual reconciliation. OTHER services can deduct separately evidenced SERVICE_COSTS; catering and medical patient fees cannot. The contract employment_type is not a tax classification. PMK 105/2025 art.4 (2026) and PMK 10/2025 as amended (2025): regular-employee DTP eligibility uses declared fixed regular gross in the statutory reference month; non-permanent monthly wages use current gross <=10m, non-monthly wages daily average <=500k. An NPWP/integrated NIK and no other DTP incentive are required. The employer flag denotes eligible KLU at the statutory reference date, not just an industry label. Monthly PPh 21 is assessed on actual month-to-date receipts at every cut-off, less withholding already settled in that month; no estimate of unpaid remuneration is withheld. Applied 2026-09-28: PMK 168/2023 art.10(1)(c): the last-period reckoning also deducts zakat or a mandatory religious contribution paid through the employer to a badan amil zakat, lembaga amil zakat or religious body formed or approved by the government — declared on the PPh 21 registration as deduction claims of category ZAKAT (this employer’s, not a prior employer’s); art.8(4): the resulting PKP is rounded down to the whole thousand rupiah. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing tax registration does not waive withholding (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU PPh art.21(1) puts the withholding on the payer, and art.21(5a) answers a recipient without an NPWP with a rate 20% higher, not with no tax; the declarations this scheme reads are still required.

elections.label: PPh 21 recipient class
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 arts.1, 12, 15–16: tax classification is declared separately from the contract label. A full-time fixed-term employee receiving regular income is REGULAR_EMPLOYEE. NON_PERMANENT_MONTHLY means output/day-based wages paid monthly.

elections.label: PTKP tax status
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): `KI` where a married woman employee shows the local government’s written statement that her husband has no income, so her PTKP includes the spouse and dependants. Unrecorded is no such statement: a married woman’s PTKP is her own.

elections.label: PTKP marital status on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(2); PMK 168/2023 art.9(4): the PTKP is the status at the start of the calendar year (for a person arriving to reside in Indonesia, the start of the arrival month). A later change applies from the next 1 January. A resident employee’s status is declared, never read from the current family record.

elections.label: PTKP dependants on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(1)(c), (2): family by blood or marriage in a direct line and adopted children, wholly supported, at most three, counted at the start of the year. Declared by the employee; the household record does not establish it.

elections.label: No NPWP and no NIK usable as NPWP
elections.description: UU PPh art.21(5a): an employee without an NPWP is withheld at a rate 20% higher. A resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP once validated (UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021; PMK 112/2022; DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024), so the surcharge applies only where neither is held. Declared for every resident employee; there is no default.

elections.label: Independent service category
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 art.12(4)–(5), Lampiran A.IV: catering uses full receipts; doctors use patient fees before hospital/clinic shares; other services exclude only separately evidenced labour, materials and third-party costs. Record those approved costs as SERVICE_COSTS deduction claims for the tax month.

elections.label: DTP fixed regular gross in the statutory reference month
elections.description: PMK 10/2025 (as amended by PMK 72/2025) and PMK 105/2025 art.4: fixed regular gross in January/the first employment month, or the applicable tourism commencement reference month in 2025. Eligibility remains anchored to that month despite later pay changes. Declare the figure for this employer and tax year.

elections.label: DTP reference tax year
elections.valid_when: !(person.terms.tax_residency == "RESIDENT" && has(person.company.facts.pph21_dtp_sector) && person.company.facts.pph21_dtp_sector && period.key >= "2025-01" && period.key < "2027-01" && scheme.elections.recipient_class == "REGULAR_EMPLOYEE" && !scheme.elections.no_tax_id) || year.start == scheme.elections.dtp_reference_year + "-01-01"

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Hari Tua (old-age savings)
authority: PP 46/2015 art.16 — 5.7% of the monthly wage, 2% from the employee and 3.7% from the employer. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AO5` = 2% (employee) and `!AR5` = 3.7% (employer); `!AE5` prints the combined 5.7%. NO CEILING: the highest-paid local employee, basic 22,380,750, is charged `AO17` 447,615 = 2% of the FULL wage, and the one foreign employee at 62,000,000 is charged `AK6` 1,240,000 = 2% of the full wage. Both would be clamped if any ceiling applied, and neither is. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): PP 46/2015 art.17(3): wages paid by the day make a month of the day’s wage × 25, whatever days were paid (`person.terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY"`). Owner rule 2026-09-28 (ID-161): PP 44/2015 art.19(1)–(2) and PP 46/2015 art.17(1)–(2) charge JKK, JKM and JHT on “Upah sebulan” — upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap as a monthly rate — and, unlike PP 45/2015 art.29(1) for JP, do not say “pada bulan yang bersangkutan”; so a monthly-paid worker's base is the contract's monthly rate (`person.terms.monthly_wage`: the basic plus the contract allowances counting toward this scheme, on the terms in force on the month's last employed day), whatever days were paid — a joiner, a leaver and a month with unpaid days are charged on the whole rate. The law is silent on an hourly-paid worker (art.19(3)–(5) name only daily, piece and weather-bound piece wages); default: the wage paid for the month's hours. Piece-rate wages use the average paid wage of the preceding 3 months, or 12 months where work depends on weather (PP 44/2015 art.19(4)–(5), PP 46/2015 art.17(4)–(5)); only months of this employment count. The first month uses the current paid wage. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing registration does not waive this charge (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; PP 46/2015 art.2(1) obliges the employer to register every worker for JHT, art.9(2) runs the contribution from the day the worker starts, and art.11(4) makes a negligent employer pay the contribution it owed. A recipient paid outside an employment relationship — a PMK 168/2023 bukan pegawai (NON_EMPLOYEE, IRREGULAR_COMMISSIONER, ACTIVITY_PARTICIPANT), a former employee or a pension withdrawal — is not a wage-earning worker of this employer: PP 44/2015 art.5(2)–(3) and PP 46/2015 art.4(2)–(3) make a worker outside an employment relationship a non-wage-earning participant who registers and pays for himself (PP 44/2015 art.11(1)), and Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) binds the employer only for its Pekerja; so that recipient class charges nothing, the lawful exclusion a NOT_REGISTERED record no longer stands in for.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Pensiun (pension)
authority: PP 45/2015 art.28 — 3% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 2% from the employer, charged on wage up to an annually adjusted ceiling (art.29). SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AN5` = 1% (employee) and `!AQ5` = 2% (employer); `!AF5` prints the combined 3%. The ceiling and its March step are read off the one employee it binds — see ID_BPJS_CEILINGS_OBSERVED. JP covers Indonesian nationals only (the rule `when`). The one foreign employee is charged 0 in both `AJ6` and `AM6` on every (FOREIGN) sheet while still paying JHT, JKK, JKM and Kesehatan. Nationality is not a `rate_selector` axis; it belongs on employment_statutory_facts — see ID_JP_FOREIGN_EXCLUSION. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23: PP 45/2015 art.15(1)–(3): the pension age is 56, 57 from 1 January 2019 and one year more every three years — 59 from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027; art.15(4): a participant who is still employed may choose to take the pension when work stops, at most three years after pension age. Contributions stop at 59 unless that choice is recorded (`scheme.elections.continue_after_pension_age`, to 62). Corrected 2026-09-28 (JP-LOCAL, supersedes R46): a missing registration does not waive JP (`unregistered_action` ASSESS, with a registration-incomplete warning). PP 45/2015 art.4(1)–(2) makes registration of every worker mandatory within 30 days of starting work, and art.5(5) obliges the negligent employer to collect and pay both the worker's and its own contributions besides the art.5(4) sanction; art.3(1) dates the start of benefit protection, and art.6 adds the employer's own liability for the benefit meanwhile — neither removes the contribution. A foreign national cannot be registered for JP (BPJS Ketenagakerjaan), so the rule `when` charges a foreigner only on a recorded registration and a NOT_REGISTERED foreigner stays at 0. Applied 2026-09-28 (ID-AUD-1): each contribution month is priced on its own wage (art.28–29(1), “pada bulan yang bersangkutan”), so a deferred earlier month paid here as back pay (`person.period.arrears`, a joiner after the cut-off) is capped at the ceiling on its own beside this month’s wage, not merged into one capped base.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja (work accident)
authority: PP 44/2015 Pasal 16(1): JKK by risk group — I 0.24%, II 0.54%, III 0.89%, IV 1.27%, V 1.74% of the wage, employer-borne. PP 44/2015 art.16(1) — an employer-only premium banded by the employer's registered work-risk group, in five groups from sangat rendah to sangat tinggi. PP 49/2023 art.16A, in force 6 October 2023, recomposes every rate by 0.14 percentage points into JKP for a wage earner required and registered in the JKP programme, giving 0.10 / 0.40 / 0.75 / 1.13 / 1.60; the art.16(1) rates 0.24 / 0.54 / 0.89 / 1.27 / 1.74 survive only for the art.16A(3) population, which this version does not model. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AS5` = 0.89% and `!AC5` = 0.24% — the art.16(1) rates for class III (sedang) and class I (sangat rendah). The actuals follow 0.89% — Sutoyo `AS8` 65,670 = 0.89% x 7,378,688 exactly, and the foreign employee `AO6` 551,800 = 0.89% x 62,000,000 exactly, at two wages three orders of magnitude apart — so the workbook's risk group is class III, not the class IV the company record states. See ID_JKK_RISK_CLASS_CONFLICT. NO CEILING: the premium is charged on the full 22,380,750 and on the full 62,000,000. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): PP 44/2015 art.19(3): wages paid by the day make a month of the day’s wage × 25, whatever days were paid (`person.terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY"`). Owner rule 2026-09-28 (ID-161): PP 44/2015 art.19(1)–(2) and PP 46/2015 art.17(1)–(2) charge JKK, JKM and JHT on “Upah sebulan” — upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap as a monthly rate — and, unlike PP 45/2015 art.29(1) for JP, do not say “pada bulan yang bersangkutan”; so a monthly-paid worker's base is the contract's monthly rate (`person.terms.monthly_wage`: the basic plus the contract allowances counting toward this scheme, on the terms in force on the month's last employed day), whatever days were paid — a joiner, a leaver and a month with unpaid days are charged on the whole rate. The law is silent on an hourly-paid worker (art.19(3)–(5) name only daily, piece and weather-bound piece wages); default: the wage paid for the month's hours. Piece-rate wages use the average paid wage of the preceding 3 months, or 12 months where work depends on weather (PP 44/2015 art.19(4)–(5), PP 46/2015 art.17(4)–(5)); only months of this employment count. The first month uses the current paid wage. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing registration does not waive this charge (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; PP 44/2015 art.4(1) obliges the employer to register every worker for JKK and JKM, art.8(2)–(3) runs the contribution from the day the worker starts and leaves the benefit on an employer that has not reported and paid, and art.10(4) makes a negligent employer pay the contribution it owed. A recipient paid outside an employment relationship — a PMK 168/2023 bukan pegawai (NON_EMPLOYEE, IRREGULAR_COMMISSIONER, ACTIVITY_PARTICIPANT), a former employee or a pension withdrawal — is not a wage-earning worker of this employer: PP 44/2015 art.5(2)–(3) and PP 46/2015 art.4(2)–(3) make a worker outside an employment relationship a non-wage-earning participant who registers and pays for himself (PP 44/2015 art.11(1)), and Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) binds the employer only for its Pekerja; so that recipient class charges nothing, the lawful exclusion a NOT_REGISTERED record no longer stands in for. Applied 2026-09-28 (ID-52): PP 7/2025 art.3–4 and art.10, extended by PP 36/2025 art.I angka 2 (art.10A) through the January 2026 contribution month: a labour-intensive enterprise with at least 50 workers registered as active BPJS Ketenagakerjaan participants, in the food, beverage and tobacco, textile and apparel, leather and leather goods, footwear, children's toy or furniture industry (art.3(3)–(4)), has its JKK cut by 50% for the contribution months February 2025 to January 2026, to I 0.120%, II 0.270%, III 0.445%, IV 0.635%, V 0.870% of Upah sebulan (art.4(1)); the entity fact `jkk_padat_karya` records that BPJS Ketenagakerjaan verified it (art.5(2)). Art.9(1) recomposes 0.120% (class I) or 0.140% (II–V) of the reduced rate into JKP, which stays inside the JKK line as the ordinary 0.14% does. Not modelled: the art.6(2) precondition of paying JKK up to January 2025, the PP 36 art.11 deadline and late-payment fallback to the PP 44/2015 rate, and the art.7 2%-a-month fine. Applied 2026-09-28 (ID-124): Permenaker 5/2021 BAB IV (arts.65–75, as amended by Permenaker 1/2025 items 34–36, which change arts.67, 69 and 75 but not art.71) covers the Pekerja Jasa Konstruksi of a Pemberi Kerja Jasa Konstruksi — daily casual (harian lepas), piece (borongan) and fixed-term (PKWT) workers (art.65) — and art.71(1) fixes their JKK at 1.74% of the monthly wage where the wage is recorded and known, whatever the employer's risk group; art.71(2) fixes JKM at 0.30%, the general rate, so JKM is unchanged. The employer is recorded as one by the company fact `jkk_jasa_konstruksi`; the worker is a PKWT (`employment.type` CONTRACT), a daily-paid worker (`terms.pay_frequency` DAILY) or a piece worker (`terms.statutory_work_category` PIECE_RATE); an open-ended (PKWTT) worker of that employer stays on its risk group (art.65 names only the three). Where the wage is not known, art.71(3)–(4) and 72 charge JKK and JKM on the construction contract value net of VAT, paid by project to BPJS Ketenagakerjaan in one sum or in stages — a project premium outside payroll, not modelled. Owner rule 2026-09-28: law silent on how an unrecorded employer status reads; default false (the risk group applies); lawful because the employer registers each project with BPJS itself (art.67) and knows it. Unchanged law, so fixed in place in every version.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Kematian (death)
authority: PP 44/2015 art.18(1) — an employer-only premium of 0.30% of the monthly wage. PP 49/2023 art.18A recomposed 0.10 points of it into JKP from 6 October 2023, but PP 6/2025 art.11, in force 7 February 2025, ended the JKM recomposition and moved JKP's remaining funding wholly onto JKK, so the rate is 0.30% again. art.34 is the JKM benefit schedule, not the rate. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AT5` = 0.3%, corroborated by `!AD5` = 0.3% in the summary block. NO CEILING: `AT17` 67,142 = 0.3% x 22,380,750 and the foreign employee `AP6` 186,000 = 0.3% x 62,000,000, both on the full wage. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): PP 44/2015 art.19(3): wages paid by the day make a month of the day’s wage × 25, whatever days were paid (`person.terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY"`). Owner rule 2026-09-28 (ID-161): PP 44/2015 art.19(1)–(2) and PP 46/2015 art.17(1)–(2) charge JKK, JKM and JHT on “Upah sebulan” — upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap as a monthly rate — and, unlike PP 45/2015 art.29(1) for JP, do not say “pada bulan yang bersangkutan”; so a monthly-paid worker's base is the contract's monthly rate (`person.terms.monthly_wage`: the basic plus the contract allowances counting toward this scheme, on the terms in force on the month's last employed day), whatever days were paid — a joiner, a leaver and a month with unpaid days are charged on the whole rate. The law is silent on an hourly-paid worker (art.19(3)–(5) name only daily, piece and weather-bound piece wages); default: the wage paid for the month's hours. Piece-rate wages use the average paid wage of the preceding 3 months, or 12 months where work depends on weather (PP 44/2015 art.19(4)–(5), PP 46/2015 art.17(4)–(5)); only months of this employment count. The first month uses the current paid wage. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing registration does not waive this charge (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; PP 44/2015 art.4(1) obliges the employer to register every worker for JKK and JKM, art.8(2)–(3) runs the contribution from the day the worker starts and leaves the benefit on an employer that has not reported and paid, and art.10(4) makes a negligent employer pay the contribution it owed. A recipient paid outside an employment relationship — a PMK 168/2023 bukan pegawai (NON_EMPLOYEE, IRREGULAR_COMMISSIONER, ACTIVITY_PARTICIPANT), a former employee or a pension withdrawal — is not a wage-earning worker of this employer: PP 44/2015 art.5(2)–(3) and PP 46/2015 art.4(2)–(3) make a worker outside an employment relationship a non-wage-earning participant who registers and pays for himself (PP 44/2015 art.11(1)), and Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) binds the employer only for its Pekerja; so that recipient class charges nothing, the lawful exclusion a NOT_REGISTERED record no longer stands in for.

name: BPJS Kesehatan (health insurance)
authority: Perpres 82/2018 art.30 as amended — 5% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 4% from the employer, charged on wage between a floor and a ceiling (Perpres 59/2024 art.32(1) and (2) — the third amendment, in force 8 May 2024 — restating the ceiling and floor; art.31 was deleted by Perpres 64/2020 and art.30(2) is the direct-payment rule). For PPU outside micro/small enterprises, art.32(2)–(3) sets the workplace UMK, with UMP as fallback; art.32(4) excludes micro/small enterprises from that floor, and art.32(5) requires a separately determined actuarial floor; Applied 2026-09-18: `by_region` carries the Kabupaten Bekasi UMK (Kepgub Jabar 2026) beside the UMP, and the company’s region names it, so the floor is the workplace UMK. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AP5` = 1% (employee) and `!AU5` = 4% (employer); `!AG5` prints the combined 5%. The 12,000,000 ceiling is read off two employees — see ID_BPJS_CEILINGS_OBSERVED. The art.30(2) FLOOR is carried by `FLOOR:MINIMUM_WAGE` against this version's `minimum_wages` map, which `company.region` keys; the source is silent on it, the lowest basic salary anywhere in the workbook being 5,938,885, so no row in the source is floored. Perpres 82/2018 art.5(3)–(4) and art.36: a further family member (a fourth child, a parent, a parent-in-law) is enrolled at the worker's election and costs 1% of the wage each, paid by the worker; carried as a rate override on the registration, never charged from the household count. One employee pays exactly 2% in every month; a dependant count is not a `rate_selector` axis. See ID_KESEHATAN_EXTRA_FAMILY_MEMBERS. art.5(3)–(4) and art.36: a further family member (a fourth child, a parent, a parent-in-law) is enrolled at the worker's election and costs 1% of the wage each, paid by the worker; carried as a rate override on the registration, never charged from the household count. EMPLOYEE_PER_DEPENDANT:20:4 charges one more employee share per head past those four; the regulation states no ceiling, so 20 is a nominal one no household reaches. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23: Perpres 82/2018 art.1 angka 2: a participant is every person, a foreigner included, who works at least six months in Indonesia — the same six-month reading JHT, JKK and JKM apply (PP 44/2015 art.1 angka 4): a foreigner on a contract shorter than six months is outside Kesehatan. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing registration does not waive this charge (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) obliges the employer to register itself and its workers “dengan membayar Iuran”, art.13(5) leaves the health benefit on an employer that has not registered and paid, and art.14(1) requires each spouse's employer to register and pay. A recipient paid outside an employment relationship — a PMK 168/2023 bukan pegawai (NON_EMPLOYEE, IRREGULAR_COMMISSIONER, ACTIVITY_PARTICIPANT), a former employee or a pension withdrawal — is not a wage-earning worker of this employer: PP 44/2015 art.5(2)–(3) and PP 46/2015 art.4(2)–(3) make a worker outside an employment relationship a non-wage-earning participant who registers and pays for himself (PP 44/2015 art.11(1)), and Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) binds the employer only for its Pekerja; so that recipient class charges nothing, the lawful exclusion a NOT_REGISTERED record no longer stands in for. Applied 2026-09-28 (ID-AUD-1): the contribution is monthly (Perpres 82/2018 art.30, art.32(1) “per bulan”), so a deferred earlier month paid here as back pay (`person.period.arrears`, a joiner after the cut-off) is floored and capped at 12,000,000 on its own beside this month’s wage, not merged into one capped base. Owner rule 2026-09-30 (tracker ID-161; Perpres 82/2018 arts.30(1), 32(1)–(2) price “Gaji atau Upah per bulan” with the UMK/UMP as its lowest bound and are silent on a part month): the base is the wage paid for the month — basic plus fixed allowances less unpaid days, the same month’s-wage reading as JP (PP 45/2015 art.29(1)) — and a month’s wage paid below the floor is lifted to the whole floor, not a prorated one; so a joiner, a leaver or a month with unpaid days whose wage paid is under the UMK is charged on the UMK (a joiner on 16 February 2026 at 12,000,000, paid 5,571,428.57 under the DKI UMP 5,729,876: 57,299 / 229,195), and a deferred joiner month paid as back pay is lifted the same way on its own.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan (job loss)
authority: PP 37/2021 Pasal 11 as amended by PP 6/2025: the JKP contribution is 0.36% of the wage capped at Rp5,000,000 (Pasal 11(7)–(8)), of which 0.22% is the central government's and 0.14% is recomposed out of the JKK contribution the employer already pays; nothing is charged on a payslip beyond JKK. PP 37/2021 art.43 as amended by PP 6/2025 art.11, in force 7 February 2025 — 0.36% of the monthly wage, of which 0.22% is borne by the Central Government and 0.14% comes from recomposing JKK (PP 49/2023 art.16A). Only that recomposed 0.14% is an employer charge: JKK class III 0.75 + JKM 0.30 + JKP 0.14 = 1.19% of wage, the same total the source workbook's 0.89 + 0.30 charges; only the composition of the payslip lines moves. JKP covers Indonesian workers under 54 at first registration with the required social-security enrolment; contribution arrears affect benefit claims but do not establish an exemption from employer registration. Neither nationality nor JKP registration is a `rate_selector` axis; both belong on employment_statutory_facts. Applied 2026-09-18: PP 37/2021 art.4 covers an Indonesian national under 54 (`citizenship`, `age`); an eligible worker recorded NOT_REGISTERED cannot be treated as exempt from JKP registration. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Corrected 2026-09-29: PP 37/2021 art.4 as amended by PP 6/2025 art.I(1) requires an Indonesian worker under 54 at registration who has an employment relationship and the prescribed JKK/JHT/JKM/JKN (and, at medium/large employers, JP) coverage. Explicit NOT_REGISTERED for that worker refuses payroll instead of erasing the duty; a foreign national or a worker already 54 at first registration remains outside JKP. Under PP 6/2025 art.I(2), JKP has no incremental employer payslip charge: its 0.14% funding is recomposed from JKK and 0.22% comes from the government; JKK is separately assessed at its full rate.

rules.when: scheme.registration_status == "NOT_REGISTERED" && person.employee.citizenship == "CITIZEN" && person.employee.age < 54.0
rules.refusal: JKP cannot be marked not registered for an Indonesian worker under 54 with an employment relationship. PP 37/2021 art.4 as amended by PP 6/2025 requires participation through the prescribed JKK, JHT, JKM and JKN programmes (and JP at medium/large employers). Resolve the actual registration and coverage before payroll.

rules.when: !(person.employee.citizenship in ["CITIZEN", "FOREIGNER"])
rules.refusal: Record the employee as an Indonesian citizen or a foreign national on the employment terms: BPJS participation of a foreign worker turns on six months’ work in Indonesia (UU 24/2011 art.14; PP 44/2015 art.1 angka 4; Perpres 82/2018 art.1 angka 2) and JKP covers citizens only (PP 37/2021 art.2). A foreigner holding a KITAP is recorded as a foreign national.

rules.when: (person.employee.citizenship != "FOREIGNER" && (person.facts.JKP.since_months > 0 ? person.employee.age - person.facts.JKP.since_months / 12.0 : person.employee.age) < 54.0) && ((((base) - 0.0 > 0.0 ? (base) - 0.0 : 0.0)) > 0.0)

name: Pajak Penghasilan Pasal 21 (income tax withholding)
authority: PP 58/2023 and PMK 168/2023, in force 1 January 2024 — for every tax period but the last, a permanent employee's withholding is the monthly average effective rate (tarif efektif rata-rata, TER) for the employee's PTKP category applied to monthly gross. Category A is PTKP TK/0 (54,000,000) and TK/1 & K/0 (58,500,000), 44 brackets; category B is TK/2 & K/1 (63,000,000) and TK/3 & K/2 (67,500,000), 40 brackets; category C is K/3 (72,000,000), 41 brackets — all transcribed from the PMK 168/2023 Lampiran. Employee JHT (2%) and JP (1%) are charged as their own schemes and are not read as a relief on this scheme’s base: PMK 168/2023 art.15 applies the TER to gross. The last tax period is the first rung: the annual UU PPh art.17(1)(a) progression on PKP = year gross − biaya jabatan (5%, at most 6,000,000; PMK 168/2023 art.10(2), which revoked PMK 250/PMK.03/2008 by art.24(a) — corrected 2026-09-28) − the year's employee JP and JHT (PMK 168/2023 art.10(1)(b), iuran terkait program pensiun dan hari tua kepada BPJS Ketenagakerjaan) − PTKP, PKP rounded down to the whole thousand (UU PPh art.17(4)), less the year's withholding, a negative charge being the refund. Employer-borne JKK, JKM and the 4% Kesehatan are additions to the taxable gross (`produced.<code>.employer` in `assessed_on`). Applied 2026-09-18: employer-borne JKK, JKM and BPJS Kesehatan premiums are additions to the gross (PMK 168/2023 art.5(1)); in the five labour-intensive sectors an employee with a monthly gross up to 10,000,000 has the PPh 21 borne by the government for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods (PMK 10/2025, PMK 105/2025; entity fact `pph21_dtp_sector`), so nothing is withheld from them. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): UU 36/2008 art.7(1): the PTKP dependant count is the dependants in a direct line of blood or marriage and adopted children, at most three (`employee.dependents_count`, capped), not the children on record; the `ptkp` election KI is PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): a married woman who shows the local government's written statement that her husband has no income is given PTKP for herself, the married status and her dependants — never the spouse's own 54,000,000, which UU 36/2008 art.7(1) grants only in a combined annual return, not in withholding (corrected 2026-09-23); PMK 168/2023 art.10(2): biaya jabatan is 5% to Rp 500,000 a month, so the year’s cap is 500,000 for each month employed (`year.months_employed`); PMK 10/2025 art.2: the Government-borne PPh 21 is for a gross fixed and regular income of at most Rp 10,000,000 in the month (`BASE` and the fixed allowances), not the whole taxable base; PP 68/2009: severance (pesangon, UPMK) is taxed at its own final rates and is outside the TER base; a non-resident is under PPh 26. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): UU 36/2008 art.21(5a) as amended by UU 7/2021 (HPP): the withholding rate for a taxpayer without an NPWP is 20% higher than for one who shows it — every rung, the year-end reckoning included, is multiplied by 1.2 under the PPH21 election `no_tax_id`. Since UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021 a resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP and DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024 applies no surcharge where a valid NIK is given, so the election is for a recipient with neither. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): PMK 168/2023 art.9(4) — the PTKP (and so the TER category and the December reckoning) is the status at the start of the calendar year. The PPH21 elections `ptkp_marital_status`, `ptkp_dependants` and `ptkp` are dated declarations whose later changes apply from the next 1 January (`change_effect` YEAR_START); an unrecorded year-start PTKP declaration refuses calculation. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): tax residence (UU PPh art.2(3)–(4)), the PTKP status and dependants at 1 January (art.7(2)), the tax identity (art.21(5a)) and, for a married employee, the gender are declared inputs; an unknown one stops the calculation rather than taking the resident, favourable or current-record reading. Applied 2026-09-25: PMK 168/2023 arts.12 and 16 and Lampiran A.III–VII: explicit recipient_class selects monthly non-permanent wages or irregular commissioners (monthly TER including the final month), independent services (Article 17 on 50% of eligible monthly gross), or activity participants, former-employee irregular payments and active pension withdrawals (Article 17 on full monthly gross). These classes do not use Article 15 annual reconciliation. OTHER services can deduct separately evidenced SERVICE_COSTS; catering and medical patient fees cannot. The contract employment_type is not a tax classification. PMK 105/2025 art.4 (2026) and PMK 10/2025 as amended (2025): regular-employee DTP eligibility uses declared fixed regular gross in the statutory reference month; non-permanent monthly wages use current gross <=10m, non-monthly wages daily average <=500k. An NPWP/integrated NIK and no other DTP incentive are required. The employer flag denotes eligible KLU at the statutory reference date, not just an industry label. Monthly PPh 21 is assessed on actual month-to-date receipts at every cut-off, less withholding already settled in that month; no estimate of unpaid remuneration is withheld. Applied 2026-09-28: PMK 168/2023 art.10(1)(c): the last-period reckoning also deducts zakat or a mandatory religious contribution paid through the employer to a badan amil zakat, lembaga amil zakat or religious body formed or approved by the government — declared on the PPh 21 registration as deduction claims of category ZAKAT (this employer’s, not a prior employer’s); art.8(4): the resulting PKP is rounded down to the whole thousand rupiah. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing tax registration does not waive withholding (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU PPh art.21(1) puts the withholding on the payer, and art.21(5a) answers a recipient without an NPWP with a rate 20% higher, not with no tax; the declarations this scheme reads are still required.

rules.refusal: Record tax residency as resident or non-resident on the employment terms before calculating Indonesian withholding: UU PPh art.2(3)–(4) makes an individual resident by residence, 183 days’ presence in twelve months, or presence with intent to reside, and sets no default for an unknown one (PPh 21 against PPh 26).

elections.label: PPh 21 recipient class
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 arts.1, 12, 15–16: tax classification is declared separately from the contract label. A full-time fixed-term employee receiving regular income is REGULAR_EMPLOYEE. NON_PERMANENT_MONTHLY means output/day-based wages paid monthly.

elections.label: PTKP tax status
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): `KI` where a married woman employee shows the local government’s written statement that her husband has no income, so her PTKP includes the spouse and dependants. Unrecorded is no such statement: a married woman’s PTKP is her own.

elections.label: PTKP marital status on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(2); PMK 168/2023 art.9(4): the PTKP is the status at the start of the calendar year (for a person arriving to reside in Indonesia, the start of the arrival month). A later change applies from the next 1 January. A resident employee’s status is declared, never read from the current family record.

elections.label: PTKP dependants on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(1)(c), (2): family by blood or marriage in a direct line and adopted children, wholly supported, at most three, counted at the start of the year. Declared by the employee; the household record does not establish it.

elections.label: No NPWP and no NIK usable as NPWP
elections.description: UU PPh art.21(5a): an employee without an NPWP is withheld at a rate 20% higher. A resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP once validated (UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021; PMK 112/2022; DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024), so the surcharge applies only where neither is held. Declared for every resident employee; there is no default.

elections.label: Independent service category
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 art.12(4)–(5), Lampiran A.IV: catering uses full receipts; doctors use patient fees before hospital/clinic shares; other services exclude only separately evidenced labour, materials and third-party costs. Record those approved costs as SERVICE_COSTS deduction claims for the tax month.

elections.label: DTP fixed regular gross in the statutory reference month
elections.description: PMK 10/2025 (as amended by PMK 72/2025) and PMK 105/2025 art.4: fixed regular gross in January/the first employment month, or the applicable tourism commencement reference month in 2025. Eligibility remains anchored to that month despite later pay changes. Declare the figure for this employer and tax year.

elections.label: DTP reference tax year
elections.valid_when: !(person.terms.tax_residency == "RESIDENT" && has(person.company.facts.pph21_dtp_sector) && person.company.facts.pph21_dtp_sector && period.key >= "2025-01" && period.key < "2027-01" && scheme.elections.recipient_class == "REGULAR_EMPLOYEE" && !scheme.elections.no_tax_id) || year.start == scheme.elections.dtp_reference_year + "-01-01"
elections.validation_message: Update the DTP reference gross and reference year for this tax year.

elections.label: Receives another government-borne PPh 21 incentive
elections.required_when: person.terms.tax_residency == "RESIDENT" && has(person.company.facts.pph21_dtp_sector) && person.company.facts.pph21_dtp_sector && period.key >= "2025-01" && period.key < "2027-01" && scheme.elections.recipient_class in ["REGULAR_EMPLOYEE", "NON_PERMANENT_MONTHLY", "NON_PERMANENT_NON_MONTHLY"] && !scheme.elections.no_tax_id
elections.description: PMK 10/2025 and PMK 105/2025 art.4: this incentive cannot be combined with another government-borne PPh 21 incentive.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Hari Tua (old-age savings)
authority: PP 46/2015 art.16 — 5.7% of the monthly wage, 2% from the employee and 3.7% from the employer. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AO5` = 2% (employee) and `!AR5` = 3.7% (employer); `!AE5` prints the combined 5.7%. NO CEILING: the highest-paid local employee, basic 22,380,750, is charged `AO17` 447,615 = 2% of the FULL wage, and the one foreign employee at 62,000,000 is charged `AK6` 1,240,000 = 2% of the full wage. Both would be clamped if any ceiling applied, and neither is. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): PP 46/2015 art.17(3): wages paid by the day make a month of the day’s wage × 25, whatever days were paid (`person.terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY"`). Owner rule 2026-09-28 (ID-161): PP 44/2015 art.19(1)–(2) and PP 46/2015 art.17(1)–(2) charge JKK, JKM and JHT on “Upah sebulan” — upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap as a monthly rate — and, unlike PP 45/2015 art.29(1) for JP, do not say “pada bulan yang bersangkutan”; so a monthly-paid worker's base is the contract's monthly rate (`person.terms.monthly_wage`: the basic plus the contract allowances counting toward this scheme, on the terms in force on the month's last employed day), whatever days were paid — a joiner, a leaver and a month with unpaid days are charged on the whole rate. The law is silent on an hourly-paid worker (art.19(3)–(5) name only daily, piece and weather-bound piece wages); default: the wage paid for the month's hours. Piece-rate wages use the average paid wage of the preceding 3 months, or 12 months where work depends on weather (PP 44/2015 art.19(4)–(5), PP 46/2015 art.17(4)–(5)); only months of this employment count. The first month uses the current paid wage. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing registration does not waive this charge (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). name: BPJS Kesehatan (health insurance)
authority: Perpres 82/2018 art.30 as amended — 5% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 4% from the employer, charged on wage between a floor and a ceiling (Perpres 59/2024 art.32(1) and (2) — the third amendment, in force 8 May 2024 — restating the ceiling and floor; art.31 was deleted by Perpres 64/2020 and art.30(2) is the direct-payment rule). For PPU outside micro/small enterprises, art.32(2)–(3) sets the workplace UMK, with UMP as fallback; art.32(4) excludes micro/small enterprises from that floor, and art.32(5) requires a separately determined actuarial floor; Applied 2026-09-18: `by_region` carries the Kabupaten Bekasi UMK (Kepgub Jabar 2026) beside the UMP, and the company’s region names it, so the floor is the workplace UMK. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AP5` = 1% (employee) and `!AU5` = 4% (employer); `!AG5` prints the combined 5%. The 12,000,000 ceiling is read off two employees — see ID_BPJS_CEILINGS_OBSERVED. The art.30(2) FLOOR is carried by `FLOOR:MINIMUM_WAGE` against this version's `minimum_wages` map, which `company.region` keys; the source is silent on it, the lowest basic salary anywhere in the workbook being 5,938,885, so no row in the source is floored. Perpres 82/2018 art.5(3)–(4) and art.36: a further family member (a fourth child, a parent, a parent-in-law) is enrolled at the worker's election and costs 1% of the wage each, paid by the worker; carried as a rate override on the registration, never charged from the household count. One employee pays exactly 2% in every month; a dependant count is not a `rate_selector` axis. See ID_KESEHATAN_EXTRA_FAMILY_MEMBERS. art.5(3)–(4) and art.36: a further family member (a fourth child, a parent, a parent-in-law) is enrolled at the worker's election and costs 1% of the wage each, paid by the worker; carried as a rate override on the registration, never charged from the household count. EMPLOYEE_PER_DEPENDANT:20:4 charges one more employee share per head past those four; the regulation states no ceiling, so 20 is a nominal one no household reaches. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Applied 2026-09-23: Perpres 82/2018 art.1 angka 2: a participant is every person, a foreigner included, who works at least six months in Indonesia — the same six-month reading JHT, JKK and JKM apply (PP 44/2015 art.1 angka 4): a foreigner on a contract shorter than six months is outside Kesehatan. UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) obliges the employer to register itself and its workers “dengan membayar Iuran”, art.13(5) leaves the health benefit on an employer that has not registered and paid, and art.14(1) requires each spouse's employer to register and pay. name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan (job loss)
authority: PP 37/2021 Pasal 11 as amended by PP 6/2025: the JKP contribution is 0.36% of the wage capped at Rp5,000,000 (Pasal 11(7)–(8)), of which 0.22% is the central government's and 0.14% is recomposed out of the JKK contribution the employer already pays; nothing is charged on a payslip beyond JKK. PP 37/2021 art.43 as amended by PP 6/2025 art.11, in force 7 February 2025 — 0.36% of the monthly wage, of which 0.22% is borne by the Central Government and 0.14% comes from recomposing JKK (PP 49/2023 art.16A). Only that recomposed 0.14% is an employer charge: JKK class III 0.75 + JKM 0.30 + JKP 0.14 = 1.19% of wage, the same total the source workbook's 0.89 + 0.30 charges; only the composition of the payslip lines moves. JKP covers Indonesian workers under 54 at first registration with the required social-security enrolment; contribution arrears affect benefit claims but do not establish an exemption from employer registration. Neither nationality nor JKP registration is a `rate_selector` axis; both belong on employment_statutory_facts. Applied 2026-09-18: PP 37/2021 art.4 covers an Indonesian national under 54 (`citizenship`, `age`); an eligible worker recorded NOT_REGISTERED cannot be treated as exempt from JKP registration. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Corrected 2026-09-29: PP 37/2021 art.4 as amended by PP 6/2025 art.I(1) requires an Indonesian worker under 54 at registration who has an employment relationship and the prescribed JKK/JHT/JKM/JKN (and, at medium/large employers, JP) coverage. Explicit NOT_REGISTERED for that worker refuses payroll instead of erasing the duty; a foreign national or a worker already 54 at first registration remains outside JKP. Under PP 6/2025 art.I(2), JKP has no incremental employer payslip charge: its 0.14% funding is recomposed from JKK and 0.22% comes from the government; JKK is separately assessed at its full rate.

name: Pajak Penghasilan Pasal 21 (income tax withholding)
authority: PP 58/2023 and PMK 168/2023, in force 1 January 2024 — for every tax period but the last, a permanent employee's withholding is the monthly average effective rate (tarif efektif rata-rata, TER) for the employee's PTKP category applied to monthly gross. Category A is PTKP TK/0 (54,000,000) and TK/1 & K/0 (58,500,000), 44 brackets; category B is TK/2 & K/1 (63,000,000) and TK/3 & K/2 (67,500,000), 40 brackets; category C is K/3 (72,000,000), 41 brackets — all transcribed from the PMK 168/2023 Lampiran. Employee JHT (2%) and JP (1%) are charged as their own schemes and are not read as a relief on this scheme’s base: PMK 168/2023 art.15 applies the TER to gross. The last tax period is the first rung: the annual UU PPh art.17(1)(a) progression on PKP = year gross − biaya jabatan (5%, at most 6,000,000; PMK 168/2023 art.10(2), which revoked PMK 250/PMK.03/2008 by art.24(a) — corrected 2026-09-28) − the year's employee JP and JHT (PMK 168/2023 art.10(1)(b), iuran terkait program pensiun dan hari tua kepada BPJS Ketenagakerjaan) − PTKP, PKP rounded down to the whole thousand (UU PPh art.17(4)), less the year's withholding, a negative charge being the refund. Employer-borne JKK, JKM and the 4% Kesehatan are additions to the taxable gross (`produced.<code>.employer` in `assessed_on`). Applied 2026-09-18: employer-borne JKK, JKM and BPJS Kesehatan premiums are additions to the gross (PMK 168/2023 art.5(1)); in the five labour-intensive sectors an employee with a monthly gross up to 10,000,000 has the PPh 21 borne by the government for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods (PMK 10/2025, PMK 105/2025; entity fact `pph21_dtp_sector`), so nothing is withheld from them. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): UU 36/2008 art.7(1): the PTKP dependant count is the dependants in a direct line of blood or marriage and adopted children, at most three (`employee.dependents_count`, capped), not the children on record; the `ptkp` election KI is PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): a married woman who shows the local government's written statement that her husband has no income is given PTKP for herself, the married status and her dependants — never the spouse's own 54,000,000, which UU 36/2008 art.7(1) grants only in a combined annual return, not in withholding (corrected 2026-09-23); PMK 168/2023 art.10(2): biaya jabatan is 5% to Rp 500,000 a month, so the year’s cap is 500,000 for each month employed (`year.months_employed`); PMK 10/2025 art.2: the Government-borne PPh 21 is for a gross fixed and regular income of at most Rp 10,000,000 in the month (`BASE` and the fixed allowances), not the whole taxable base; PP 68/2009: severance (pesangon, UPMK) is taxed at its own final rates and is outside the TER base; a non-resident is under PPh 26. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): UU 36/2008 art.21(5a) as amended by UU 7/2021 (HPP): the withholding rate for a taxpayer without an NPWP is 20% higher than for one who shows it — every rung, the year-end reckoning included, is multiplied by 1.2 under the PPH21 election `no_tax_id`. Since UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021 a resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP and DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024 applies no surcharge where a valid NIK is given, so the election is for a recipient with neither. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): PMK 168/2023 art.9(4) — the PTKP (and so the TER category and the December reckoning) is the status at the start of the calendar year. The PPH21 elections `ptkp_marital_status`, `ptkp_dependants` and `ptkp` are dated declarations whose later changes apply from the next 1 January (`change_effect` YEAR_START); an unrecorded year-start PTKP declaration refuses calculation. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): tax residence (UU PPh art.2(3)–(4)), the PTKP status and dependants at 1 January (art.7(2)), the tax identity (art.21(5a)) and, for a married employee, the gender are declared inputs; an unknown one stops the calculation rather than taking the resident, favourable or current-record reading. Applied 2026-09-25: PMK 168/2023 arts.12 and 16 and Lampiran A.III–VII: explicit recipient_class selects monthly non-permanent wages or irregular commissioners (monthly TER including the final month), independent services (Article 17 on 50% of eligible monthly gross), or activity participants, former-employee irregular payments and active pension withdrawals (Article 17 on full monthly gross). These classes do not use Article 15 annual reconciliation. OTHER services can deduct separately evidenced SERVICE_COSTS; catering and medical patient fees cannot. The contract employment_type is not a tax classification. PMK 105/2025 art.4 (2026) and PMK 10/2025 as amended (2025): regular-employee DTP eligibility uses declared fixed regular gross in the statutory reference month; non-permanent monthly wages use current gross <=10m, non-monthly wages daily average <=500k. An NPWP/integrated NIK and no other DTP incentive are required. The employer flag denotes eligible KLU at the statutory reference date, not just an industry label. Monthly PPh 21 is assessed on actual month-to-date receipts at every cut-off, less withholding already settled in that month; no estimate of unpaid remuneration is withheld. Applied 2026-09-28: PMK 168/2023 art.10(1)(c): the last-period reckoning also deducts zakat or a mandatory religious contribution paid through the employer to a badan amil zakat, lembaga amil zakat or religious body formed or approved by the government — declared on the PPh 21 registration as deduction claims of category ZAKAT (this employer’s, not a prior employer’s); art.8(4): the resulting PKP is rounded down to the whole thousand rupiah. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing tax registration does not waive withholding (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU PPh art.21(1) puts the withholding on the payer, and art.21(5a) answers a recipient without an NPWP with a rate 20% higher, not with no tax; the declarations this scheme reads are still required.

elections.label: PPh 21 recipient class
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 arts.1, 12, 15–16: tax classification is declared separately from the contract label. A full-time fixed-term employee receiving regular income is REGULAR_EMPLOYEE. NON_PERMANENT_MONTHLY means output/day-based wages paid monthly.

elections.label: PTKP tax status
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 art.9(3): `KI` where a married woman employee shows the local government’s written statement that her husband has no income, so her PTKP includes the spouse and dependants. Unrecorded is no such statement: a married woman’s PTKP is her own.

elections.label: PTKP marital status on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(2); PMK 168/2023 art.9(4): the PTKP is the status at the start of the calendar year (for a person arriving to reside in Indonesia, the start of the arrival month). A later change applies from the next 1 January. A resident employee’s status is declared, never read from the current family record.

elections.label: PTKP dependants on 1 January
elections.description: UU PPh art.7(1)(c), (2): family by blood or marriage in a direct line and adopted children, wholly supported, at most three, counted at the start of the year. Declared by the employee; the household record does not establish it.

elections.label: No NPWP and no NIK usable as NPWP
elections.description: UU PPh art.21(5a): an employee without an NPWP is withheld at a rate 20% higher. A resident’s NIK serves as the NPWP once validated (UU KUP art.2(1a) as amended by UU 7/2021; PMK 112/2022; DJP PENG-6/PJ.09/2024), so the surcharge applies only where neither is held. Declared for every resident employee; there is no default.

elections.label: Independent service category
elections.description: PMK 168/2023 art.12(4)–(5), Lampiran A.IV: catering uses full receipts; doctors use patient fees before hospital/clinic shares; other services exclude only separately evidenced labour, materials and third-party costs. Record those approved costs as SERVICE_COSTS deduction claims for the tax month.

elections.label: DTP fixed regular gross in the statutory reference month
elections.description: PMK 10/2025 (as amended by PMK 72/2025) and PMK 105/2025 art.4: fixed regular gross in January/the first employment month, or the applicable tourism commencement reference month in 2025. Eligibility remains anchored to that month despite later pay changes. Declare the figure for this employer and tax year.

elections.label: DTP reference tax year

authority: PP 68/2009 art.2–4: severance pay (uang pesangon, uang penghargaan masa kerja) paid at once is subject to a final PPh 21 — 0% to Rp 50,000,000, 5% to 100,000,000, 15% to 500,000,000, 25% above — separately from the monthly TER withholding; the tiers accumulate over payments within two years, which this row reads as one payment. Applied 2026-09-23: PP 68/2009 art.1 angka 4 defines uang pesangon as income paid, under whatever name and in whatever form, in connection with the end of service or termination, including UPMK and UPH; uang pisah is paid only on termination (PP 35/2021 arts.50–54), so it is in this final base and outside the TER. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): uang kompensasi PKWT is paid when the fixed-term agreement ends (PP 35/2021 art.15(2)), in connection with the end of service, so it is in this final base too. Applied 2026-09-28: the uang penggantian hak PP 68/2009 art.1 angka 4 names includes untaken, unlapsed annual leave (PP 35/2021 art.40(4)(a)), so leave cashed out on or after the last day of work (`ENCASHMENT` once `employment.exit_date` has passed) is in this final base and out of the PPH21 TER/annual base; an in-service cash-out stays ordinary income. Applied 2026-09-28 (re-read of the signed PP 68/2009 on jdih.kemnaker.go.id, PP_No_68_2009.pdf): the four uang pesangon bands are art.4 (art.5 is the two-band scale for pension benefit, THT and JHT). Art.1 angka 3 limits “Pegawai” to a resident individual, so a non-resident’s separation pay is PPh 26 at 20% of gross (PMK 168/2023 arts.5(1), 12(9), 14(1)), not this row. Art.2(2) and its elucidation (“dihitung sebagai satu kesatuan untuk pengenaan pajaknya”): payments made within two calendar years count as paid at once, so the bands run on this employer’s severance base of the previous and current calendar years (`scheme.last_year`, `scheme.year_to_date`) plus this one, less what those payments already withheld. Applied 2026-09-28 (PP 68/2009 art.6(1)–(3) and its elucidation, same signed text): a part paid in the third calendar year or later, counted from the tax year of this employer’s first charged severance base (`scheme.first_year`), is not joined to the earlier parts: it is withheld at the UU PPh art.17(1)(a) rates as amended by UU 7/2021 on the gross of that calendar year’s parts (`scheme.year_to_date` plus this one), less what that year already withheld; that withholding is not final and is creditable as a prepayment in the recipient’s annual return (art.6(2)), and art.21(5a)’s 120% applies without an NPWP (art.6(3), election `no_tax_id`). Elucidation: 5% × 50,000,000 = 2,500,000, 120% of it = 3,000,000. Ceiling: the year gross is this scheme’s severance parts; other income paid in that year is withheld under PPH21 and is not added (the elucidation’s example assumes none). A new severance after an earlier one (rehire) is joined to it, and counts its third year from it. Applied 2026-09-28 (R46): a missing tax registration does not waive withholding (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU PPh art.21(1) puts the withholding on the payer, and art.21(5a) answers a recipient without an NPWP with a rate 20% higher, not with no tax; the declarations this scheme reads are still required.
